params.fee_defect: commands/rules.py:100 calls backtest(rule, candles) with no fee_pct, taking the maker default 0.006, on a simulator that fills market-style at next-bar open -- which config.paperforward.yaml:111-117 itself calls taker and prices at 0.012. The printed output names no fee. Same 0.006 in cli.py::_SIM_FEE_PCT, portfolio_sim.run and paper.py::_DEFAULT_FEE_PCT, so promotion.can_promote has been gating on half-cost stats. Recommended as a follow-up issue; NOT fixed in this PR.
params.finding: Same rule, same constructor defaults, same cached candles, ONE_DAY -> ONE_HOUR. RESULT 1 -- the promotion floor is REACHABLE: hourly trade counts are 195-274 against 4-13 daily over the SAME calendar window (BTC 1850 daily bars and 44393 hourly bars are both 5.07 years), so 18 of 19 assets clear min_trades=100 outright. config.live-sandbox.yaml's '100 trades in ~39 years' (BTC) / '~84 years' (ADA) becomes 1.85 / 2.11 years, and the sample already exists on disk. The daily trade rate spans 1.19-3.18/yr across the five live assets (2.7x) while the hourly rate spans 47.3-54.1/yr (1.14x): the rate is set by the bar clock, not the asset. PAXG's n=61 is the sole miss and is a history-length artifact -- 11025 hourly bars (native-USD listing 2025-05-08); at its own realized rate it crosses 100 after ~294 more days. RESULT 2 -- and the rule FAILS ON EDGE, not on sample size: at the backtest's own default fee_pct=0.006, PF runs 0.270-1.042 with 18 of 19 below 1.0; win rates cluster 15-27%. The five live incumbents score 0.584/0.534/0.479/0.318/0.316 against the daily figures of 11.44/5.52/1.21/1.61/3.25 recorded in config.live-sandbox.yaml on n=8/6/13/13/4. RESULT 3 -- the ONE apparent winner is a FEE ARTIFACT: commands/rules.py::_run_backtest calls backtest(rule, candles) with no fee_pct and takes the maker default 0.006, while config.paperforward.yaml declares taker_pct 0.012 and states in its own comment that taker is the sim's default because it fills market-style at next-bar open. Round-trip friction 1.30% -> 2.50% of notional (1.92x). Re-run at 0.012: ZEC 1.042 -> 0.736, and ZERO of 19 assets clear PF 1.0. Deltas of 0.17-0.31 for a 1.2pp cost change mean the gross move per trade is the same order as the cost -- these are cost-dominated results. The same 0.006 is pinned in cli.py::_SIM_FEE_PCT, portfolio_sim.run and paper.py::_DEFAULT_FEE_PCT, so the edge table, the portfolio sim, the paper-forward's realized record and promotion.can_promote itself have all been priced at half the realistic cost. NOT FIXED HERE. RESULT 4 -- independent convergence: DOGE daily PF 1.489 on n=12 is the field's best daily result and the sole performance basis for its shortlisting, but ONE trade is 63% of gross profit; 1.489 x (1 - 0.63) = 0.551 against a HOURLY PF of 0.558 on n=261. Two methods sharing no data beyond the price series land 0.007 apart. CONSEQUENCE: the config.live-sandbox.yaml standing exception's PREMISE ('this strategy cannot reach it; waiting for the gate is not a slower path to the same place, it is no path') is FALSE as written; its CONCLUSION may still hold on the caps, the guards, and the fact that the live rules trade the daily clock. Nothing demoted, nothing reconfigured, no config edited.

params.harness: keel/strategy/backtest.py::backtest, shipped and unmodified, over Repository.get_candles(product_id, ONE_HOUR) against the paper-forward candle cache. No new instrument and no driver script -- the negative result comes off the same code path as every published positive one.
params.limitation: STRONGEST OBJECTION, stated up front in the document rather than buried: these are daily-tuned parameters on an hourly clock. turtle_breakout's source comments read 'entry_lookback: int = 40, # Donchian-high entry (days)' and 'atr_period: int = 20, # 20 days = Turtle's N'; hourly they become 40 hours and 20 hours, and Turtle's N is no longer N. The rule hard-codes self.granularity = Granularity.ONE_DAY and backtest keys the per-bar window by _rule_trading_tf(rule), so the hourly series arrives under the ONE_DAY key and the rule cannot tell -- no error, no warning, no field recording the clock. A fair reading is therefore 'daily-tuned turtle does not transfer to an hourly clock', NOT 'trend following fails on crypto'. Untouched by the objection: the trade-count result (arithmetic about the bar clock, true of any configuration that reaches the floor), the fee defect (wrong at every granularity), and the DOGE decomposition (a pure daily-bar result). The resolving experiment -- rerun with parameters SCALED to the hourly clock, ~960 bars for a 40-day channel -- has not been run and is recommended as a follow-up.

params.answer: The objection is correct and does not rescue the rule. Re-tuning lifts mean PF 0.419 -> 0.634 (+51%) and the longest lookbacks win as wall-clock theory predicts, but 0 of 144 configs average PF > 1.0 across six assets and 0 of 864 cells clear PF 1.0 at n >= 100.

params.fee_model: taker 1.2% on both legs, slippage 0.0005 -- STRICTER than the project's own gate, which still prices 0.6% at backtest.py:171, portfolio_sim.py:225, paper.py:46 and cli.py:1691. Numbers here are not comparable to `keel rules backtest` output.
params.grid_pre_declared: Grid was declared in the script docstring before the run and is unchanged; no cells added after seeing results, none dropped. Hence provenance a_priori.
params.question: Does ANY hourly-appropriate parameter set give turtle_breakout a positive edge? Tests the strongest objection to hourly-turtle-granularity-2026-08-11: that entry_lookback=40 means 40 HOURS on hourly bars, so the params were never tuned for this granularity.
params.recommended_next: (a) ZEC regime split, 8 configs, pre-surge vs surge window. (b) maker-fill model with tuned params -- halving round-trip friction 2.50% -> 1.30% is worth more than this entire grid (baseline at maker = 0.640 mean vs best-of-144 at taker = 0.634). (c) NOT another parameter sweep.
params.structural_finding: Edge and sample size move in opposite directions: Spearman(mean PF, mean n) = -0.77 over the 144 configs. The configs closest to break-even are exactly the ones that cannot clear min_trades=100. Not a tuning problem; the shape of the strategy.
params.validation: Screening result only. No walk-forward, no CSCV/PBO, no deflated Sharpe, one rule, one grid, 6 of 19 assets, one window, same cached candles as everything else.
params.winning_cells: All 8 cells above PF 1.0 are ZEC-USD, n 49-67, all adx_threshold=25, all at entry_lookback 240 or 336. ZEC's 180-day median daily quote volume is ~30x its full-history median ($37.9M vs $1,229,309) and its close ran 36.92 -> 510.43 in 2025H2; the other five assets all trade BELOW their own historical median. Probably regime, not edge -- but no regime split was run, so this is argued, not measured.
